lede.headline: California voters reject billionaire wealth tax
lede.dek: The Associated Press called Proposition 40 defeated on Nov. 9 after a campaign where Google co-founder Sergey Brin gave more than $100 million to the opposition, which raised over $300 million in all.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: California voters reject billionaire wealth tax
stories.move: The Associated Press called California's Proposition 40 defeated on Nov. 9, nearly a week after Election Day as mail ballots were counted. The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the personal assets of residents worth more than $1 billion, with most revenue going to healthcare. A group opposing the measure raised more than $300 million; Google co-founder Sergey Brin gave more than $100 million of that total, the New York Times reported.
stories.why: It's the clearest sign yet that California billionaires can still out-spend a populist tax measure even in a state that leans heavily Democratic, and it removes, for now, a template other states' wealth-tax backers were watching.
stories.bear: The fight isn't fully over: a companion measure to bar future wealth taxes, Proposition 42, was still being counted as a narrower contest, and backers of Prop 40 could try again in a future election.
stories.watch: Final certification of both propositions by the California Secretary of State, and whether similar wealth-tax measures appear on other states' 2027 or 2028 ballots.

stories.headline: Berkshire sells ¥182.3 billion in new yen bonds
stories.move: Berkshire Hathaway priced a five-tranche yen bond offering on Nov. 13 totaling ¥182.3 billion (about $1.2 billion), an SEC filing showed. The notes mature between 2029 and 2056, with coupons from 2.624% to 4.571%, and are rated Aa2/AA. The company will receive about ¥182.0 billion in proceeds; settlement is set for Nov. 19. The filing doesn't state a use of proceeds.
stories.why: Berkshire has used yen debt for years to help fund its stakes in Japanese trading houses, so a fresh bond sale signals it's still comfortable borrowing cheaply in yen even with its cash pile already near $357 billion.
stories.bear: The filing itself doesn't say what the money is for, so any link to new Japanese stock purchases is speculation until Berkshire's next 13F or annual filing shows it.
stories.watch: Berkshire's next 13F filing, due by mid-February, for any change in its Japanese trading-house stakes.

stories.headline: Page family trusts file to sell $148 million in Alphabet stock
stories.move: Three trusts tied to Larry Page — the Lawrence Page Trust, Trust II and Trust III — filed SEC Form 144 notices on Nov. 12 for a combined 507,680 Alphabet shares, split evenly between Class A and Class C stock, worth about $148.3 million at the filings' reference prices. The sales are set under a trading plan the trusts adopted Nov. 30, 2020.
stories.why: A Form 144 is only a notice of intent to sell under a pre-existing plan, not a confirmed sale, but the combined size shows continued, steady share sales from Page's holding structure even as Alphabet stock has rallied this year.
stories.bear: Regular sales under a multi-year 10b5-1-style plan are routine for insiders with large stakes and don't necessarily reflect any view on Alphabet's prospects.
stories.watch: Form 4 filings from the same trusts confirming the sales actually went through.

stories.headline: Newsmax swings to profit on a one-time fee
stories.move: Newsmax reported Nov. 12 that third-quarter revenue rose 52.5% year over year to $69.0 million, which included a one-time $14.0 million service-revenue termination fee; excluding that item, revenue grew 21.6% to $55.0 million. Net income was $15.2 million, versus a $4.1 million loss a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA was $19.0 million. The company kept its underlying full-year revenue guidance at $212 million to $216 million.
stories.why: Newsmax, in which Interactive Brokers founder Thomas Peterffy holds roughly a quarter of the shares, needed a cleaner quarter after a post-IPO slide; the swing to profit and maintained guidance give the stock a reason to stabilize.
stories.bear: More than a quarter of the quarter's revenue growth came from a one-time fee that won't repeat, and digital revenue actually fell 4.1% even as broadcasting grew.
stories.watch: Whether Newsmax's underlying (ex-one-time-item) revenue growth holds up without one-time items in the fourth quarter.
stories.source: SEC EDGAR filing (Newsmax Q3 2026 earnings release)

stories.headline: Fast Retailing posts record profit as Uniqlo sales jump
stories.move: Fast Retailing, the Uniqlo parent chaired by Tadashi Yanai, reported Nov. 10 that revenue for the business year ended in August rose 16.6% to 3.96 trillion yen, with net profit up 25.3% to a record 542.52 billion yen. Yanai said the company's longstanding goal of 10 trillion yen in annual sales is "now within our sights."
stories.why: The record result shows Uniqlo's international expansion is still outrunning the broader apparel market, at a time several Western retailers have struggled with soft demand.
stories.bear: A weak yen flatters yen-denominated results for a company with large overseas sales; the growth rate in constant currency isn't broken out in the release.
stories.watch: Fast Retailing's first-quarter results for the new fiscal year, typically reported in early January.

stories.headline: Adelson sells her Mavericks stake to the Dumont family
stories.move: Patrick and Sivan Dumont bought Miriam Adelson's majority stake in the Dallas Mavericks, giving the Dumonts 69% of the ownership group, ESPN and The Athletic reported; Fox4 and other outlets confirmed the deal this month. Adelson, whose family controls Las Vegas Sands, had held the stake since buying it from Mark Cuban in December 2023; Patrick Dumont, her son-in-law and the Sands' CEO, had served as the team's governor throughout. Cuban keeps his 27% stake and an option to buy up to 20% more from the Dumonts at the original valuation.
stories.why: It consolidates control of the Mavericks in the hands of the Dumonts, who've run the team day to day since 2023, and ends Adelson's direct ownership stake in an NBA franchise.
stories.bear: Neither side has disclosed a price for the shares, so there's no way yet to judge whether Adelson got a good return on her 2023 purchase.
stories.watch: Any NBA board of governors approval and whether Cuban exercises his option to buy more of the team.

stories.headline: ByteDance plans a Muse-like AI agent within weeks
stories.move: ByteDance is preparing to launch an AI video assistant similar to Meta's Muse within weeks, Bloomberg reported Nov. 11, citing people familiar with the plans. At an internal all-hands meeting, co-founder Zhang Yiming told staff ByteDance could compete with leading AI labs "at the cutting edge" but not before 2029 or 2030.
stories.why: It shows ByteDance racing to match Meta and other rivals in AI video tools even as its own founder sets a long timeline for catching the frontier labs.
stories.bear: The report relies on anonymous sources and ByteDance hasn't confirmed a product or date; Bloomberg said the company didn't respond to a request for comment.
stories.watch: Whether ByteDance actually ships the assistant in the "coming weeks" window the report described.

stories.headline: Koch's holding company sells more Ibotta stock
stories.move: KDT Ibotta Holdings, an entity tied to Koch, Inc., sold 275,000 Ibotta shares over Nov. 11-12 for roughly $16.4 million at prices between $58.97 and $60.38, an SEC Form 4 filed Nov. 13 showed. It's the latest in a series of sales from the stake; the same entity sold 200,000 shares over Nov. 9-10 and another 200,000 over Nov. 5-6.
stories.why: The steady pace of sales — now three filings in two weeks — suggests a systematic wind-down of Koch's position in the cashback-rewards app rather than a one-off trade.
stories.bear: Without a disclosed trading plan, it's not possible to say how much of the original stake is left or when the selling might stop.
stories.watch: Whether the pace of sales continues at a similar size in the next Form 4 filing.

watch: Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results Nov. 17; a closed-door briefing for House committees on Jensen Huang's conduct had been requested for Nov. 18.
Berkshire Hathaway's new yen notes settle Nov. 19.
California's Secretary of State has yet to certify final results for Propositions 40 and 42.
quickHits: SoftBank's Masayoshi Son sold his Nvidia shares in October, before reports linked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to an alleged Chinese intelligence contact, the AP reported Nov. 10.
memo: A pre-set trading plan explains most insider sales (Page, Koch); check the plan's adoption date before reading a sale as a signal about the company.
Watch for one-time items inside a good-looking headline growth number, the way Newsmax's 52.5% revenue growth shrinks to 21.6% once a one-time fee is stripped out.
Large companies still borrow in foreign currencies like yen for cheap, long-dated financing even while holding enormous cash piles; it's a financing choice, not a sign of distress.
